definitions.name: Maximal common bijection group
definitions.construction: \(G_\star=\{f\in\operatorname{Bij}(\mathcal X_{m,K}):P_R(f(C))=P_R(C)\ \text{for every}\ C\in\mathcal X_{m,K}\ \text{and}\ R\in\mathcal R_0(n,K)\}\)

definitions.name: Rectangular hypergeometric stabilizer handle
definitions.construction: Start from diagonal response tables and two-unit zero-effect switches under the fixed \((n_1,n_0)\) coefficient kernel, derive the resulting falling-factorial invariants of the two arm histograms, and compute the stabilizer of the full coefficient-vector map before constructing sparse legal separators.

statements.statement: For every \(C=(h,g)\in\mathcal X_{m,K}\) with \(r=h+g\), the diagonal response table \(D_r\) is legal and \(W_{D_r}(C)=Q_r(h)=\prod_{a\in\mathcal A_K}\binom{r_a}{h_a}\). If a profile has pooled histogram different from \(r\), its count under \(D_r\) is zero.
statements.justification: This is the sharp-null sanity reduction and the first coefficient probe: pooled histograms and their ordinary multivariate-hypergeometric weights are observable invariants.
statements.gap: The formula is standard hypergeometric bookkeeping, used here as a supporting reduction rather than claimed against \cite{RigdonHudgens2015} or \cite{LiDing2016}.
statements.consumer: It gives an exact fast pre-screen that discards profile comparisons already separated by a diagonal schedule.

statements.statement: For every \(m\geq1\) and \(K\geq2\), if \(C\sim C'\), then \(C'=C\) or \(C'=C^\top\). More precisely, after Proposition 1 fixes \(r\), the legal symmetric switch \(D_{r-e_a-e_b}+E_{ab}+E_{ba}\) implies \((h_a-g_a)(h_b-g_b)=(h'_a-g'_a)(h'_b-g'_b)\) for every distinct supported \(a,b\), and hence the two arm-imbalance vectors agree up to a common sign.
statements.justification: The switch identity turns an exponential family of nuisance schedules into an arm-imbalance outer product, reducing the classification to the survival of transposition.
statements.gap: Generic orbit theory in \cite{HemerikGoeman2018} starts from invariance; it does not provide the causal zero-sum switches that force this two-point reduction.
statements.consumer: It converts any future implementation of equivalence checking from comparison over all profiles to tests of a profile and its arm transpose.

statements.statement: For every \(R\in\mathcal R_0(n,K)\), \(W_R(C_+)=W_R(C_-)=1\) if \(R=mE_{LL}+mE_{00}\), and \(W_R(C_+)=W_R(C_-)=0\) otherwise.
statements.justification: Endpoint saturation is the only universal nonbinary tie and supplies the exact probability bound behind the non-orbit corner test.
statements.gap: The compatible-table literature in \cite{RigdonHudgens2015} enumerates nuisance schedules for inference but does not isolate this schedule-universal endpoint identity.
statements.consumer: It yields an analytic weak-null p-value with granularity \(\binom{2m}{m}^{-1}\), avoiding nuisance enumeration for this rare event.

statements.statement: For every \(m\geq1\): if \(K=2\), then \(C\sim C'\) if and only if \(C'=C\) or \(C'=C^\top\); if \(K\geq3\), then \(C\sim C'\) if and only if \(C'=C\) or \(\{C,C'\}=\{C_+,C_-\}\). Whenever \(C\not\sim C'\), one has \(d(C,C')\leq3\).
statements.justification: The theorem gives the complete outcome-alphabet phase change in exact weak-null symmetry and a uniform constructive certificate for every nonequivalence.
statements.gap: The closest results are the i.i.d. finite-support criterion of \cite{DutzZhang2026} and the asymptotic fixed-population theorem of \cite{WuDing2021}; neither classifies the all-schedule hypergeometric kernel.
statements.consumer: DeclareDesign's balanced \(250\)-of-\(500\) binary reply audit can use this theorem to state exactly which histogram transformations, rather than which sharp-null imputations, are justified by the weak average-effect null.

statements.statement: Let \(K\geq3\), \(m\geq3\), \(1\leq i\leq m-1\), and \(2i\neq m\). For \(C=((m-i)e_0+ie_L,\ ie_0+(m-i)e_L)\) and \(C'=C^\top\), one has \(d(C,C')=3\).
statements.justification: This proves that the cubic endpoint gadget is not an artifact of the construction: three heterogeneous units are necessary in general.
statements.gap: Neither exact binary test inversion in \cite{RigdonHudgens2015} nor generic group testing in \cite{HemerikGoeman2018} studies the sparse legal-schedule certificate number.
statements.consumer: The result bounds the smallest adversarial schedule that a software unit test must include to audit the proposed symmetry classifier.

statements.statement: The group \(G_\star\) is the direct product of the symmetric groups on the \(\sim\)-classes. Consequently, for \(K=2\), \(G_\star\cong(S_2)^{\binom{m+1}{2}}\); for \(K\geq3\), \(G_\star\cong S_2\), acting only on \(\{C_+,C_-\}\).
statements.justification: This translates the probability partition into the largest schedule-universal transformation group without presupposing the group.
statements.gap: \cite{HemerikGoeman2018} establishes exact testing for a specified invariant group; the new input is the maximal group forced by the composite causal null.
statements.consumer: It supplies a precise validation target for any software option advertised as a weak-null common-invariance randomization test.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(G\leq G_\star\), every fixed statistic \(T:\mathcal X_{m,K}\to\mathbb R\), and every \(C\in\mathcal X_{m,K}\), the conventional nonrandomized group-rank p-value satisfies \(p_G(C)\in\{1/2,1\}\) and \(\Pr_R\{p_G(C)\leq\alpha\}\leq\alpha\) for every \(R\in\mathcal R_0(n,K)\).
statements.justification: The theorem states the exact inferential consequence of maximal common symmetry and no broader impossibility claim.
statements.gap: The rank argument is informed by \cite{HemerikGoeman2018}; the substantive input is the newly derived orbit-size frontier from the alphabet-frontier theorem.
statements.consumer: For the binary reply audit, it shows why conventional common-orbit ranks cannot reproduce the usual \(5\%\) HC2 or robust-\(t\) workflow studied by \cite{ZhaoDing2021}.

statements.statement: For every \(K\geq2\), the function \(p_{\mathrm{corner}}\) satisfies \(\Pr_R\{p_{\mathrm{corner}}(C)\leq\alpha\}\leq\alpha\) for every \(R\in\mathcal R_0(n,K)\) and every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\). Its nontrivial value is \(\binom{2m}{m}^{-1}\), which can be strictly below \(1/2\).
statements.justification: This analytic counterpoint prevents the group classification from being misread as nonexistence of all other exact weak-null tests.
statements.gap: Exact binary procedures in \cite{RigdonHudgens2015} already show that nuisance-aware tests can exist; this proposition isolates a particularly transparent non-orbit rule inside the present model.
statements.consumer: It tells DeclareDesign developers that an exact weak-null module may use analytic calibration or nuisance maximization even though common-orbit ranks are coarse.

statements.statement: Using the rectangular hypergeometric stabilizer handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{unbal}}\), characterize the schedule-universal profile-equivalence classes and maximal common bijection group for complete randomization with \(n_1\neq n_0\), and determine the smallest uniform heterogeneous-unit separator bound as a function of \((n_1,n_0,K)\).
statements.justification: Unequal allocation removes treatment complementation, so the first identity supporting balanced transposition disappears and a genuinely new frontier is required.
statements.gap: \cite{ChungRomano2013} treats unequal proportions asymptotically and \cite{AronowChangLopatto2025} finds a computational balance split, but neither gives the exact fixed-schedule equivalence partition.
statements.consumer: The answer would extend the software validation rule to trials whose realized or planned treatment count is not one half of the population.

sampling_model.units: The \(n=2m\) labeled units have fixed no-interference potential-outcome pairs summarized by \(R\in\mathcal R_0(n,K)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly \(m\) units receive treatment and \(m\) receive control.
sampling_model.overlap: Every labeled assignment in \(\mathcal Z_m\) has probability \(\binom{2m}{m}^{-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no estimated nuisance. Exact claims are uniform over the finite set \(\mathcal R_0(n,K)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 3.1 characterizes invariant bijections for i.i.d. finite-support samples through equality of product probability masses.
Theorem 1 gives asymptotically conservative weak-null validity for a studentized Fisher randomization test on fixed finite populations.
Theorem 1 gives finite-sample level control for rank tests under an assumed finite-group invariance.
The paper constructs finite-sample exact confidence sets for the binary average treatment effect by prediction and randomization-test inversion.
Balanced binary exact confidence sets can be computed with \(O(n\log n)\) permutation tests, compared with \(O(n^2)\) generally.
Robustly studentized interacted OLS Fisher tests are finite-sample exact under the sharp null and asymptotically valid under the weak null.

tldr: Balanced complete randomization leaves the exact law under a weak average-effect null dependent on an unknown fixed response schedule. The proposal classifies the transformations that nevertheless preserve every such law. Binary outcomes retain every arm-transpose pair; three or more equally spaced levels destroy all nontrivial pairs except the two opposing endpoint-saturation profiles. The proof is certified by legal schedules with at most three heterogeneous units, and three are necessary in general. The induced maximal group makes conventional nonrandomized orbit-rank p-values take only the values \(1/2\) and \(1\), while an explicit corner p-value shows that this is not an impossibility claim for other exact tests.

project_justification.gap: Weak-null randomization theory supplies asymptotic studentization or exact inversion over compatible binary schedules, while general permutation theory assumes a null-invariant group. The literature does not identify the probability-equivalence partition induced by all fixed zero-average-effect schedules.
project_justification.niche: A finite outcome alphabet turns the missing-schedule problem into an exact multivariate-hypergeometric coefficient system whose common symmetries can be classified rather than assumed.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the complete alphabet-indexed equivalence frontier, the maximal common bijection group, and an optimal sparse-separator theorem, then states the resulting orbit-rank limitation with an explicit non-orbit exact counterexample.

related_work: \cite{WuDing2021} frames the weak-null obstacle through missing potential outcomes and obtains asymptotic control by studentization. \cite{HemerikGoeman2018} supplies the orbit-counting logic once a transformation group is known. \cite{DutzZhang2026} characterizes invariant bijections for i.i.d. finite-support samples, whose product-mass polynomial differs from the fixed-schedule hypergeometric kernel here. \cite{RigdonHudgens2015} and \cite{LiDing2016} construct exact binary average-effect confidence sets by compatible-table reasoning rather than a common group. \cite{AronowChangLopatto2025} proves a balanced computational acceleration for that inversion problem. \cite{ChungRomano2013} treats unequal group proportions through asymptotic multinomial--hypergeometric coupling. \cite{ZhaoDing2021} gives the robust-\(t\) weak-null workflow that motivates the applied audit, but its guarantee is asymptotic under the weak null.
technical_internal_limitation: The cubic endpoint identity and the two-heterogeneous-unit lower-bound case split remain proof obligations, not cited facts. An independent raw-assignment audit at \(K=3,n=6\) obtained counts \(1\) and \(0\) for the cubic witness and exhaustively confirmed equality under every legal schedule with at most two heterogeneous units. This finite check supports but does not prove the all-size theorem.
honest_scope: The headline concerns fixed no-interference schedules, balanced complete randomization, histogram-measurable common bijections, and equally spaced finite alphabets. It does not classify every exact weak-null test, validate a particular sharp-null permutation statistic, or cover covariate-adaptive, stratified, clustered, or unequal-arm designs. Under a diagonal sharp-null schedule, Proposition 1 reduces exactly to the familiar multivariate-hypergeometric law. Unequal allocation is retained as Open-ended Question 1 because treatment complementation no longer preserves the assignment space.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Theorem 1 and its finite-population variance argument, Appendix A2, and the Discussion were read. The paper isolates the missing-potential-outcome obstruction under a weak null and replaces finite-sample identification of the randomization law by asymptotic studentization.
seed_details.kernel: For every balanced population size and every equally spaced finite outcome alphabet, classify the observable histogram pairs having equal randomization probability under every zero-average-effect response table, and derive the maximal common action from that classification.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The first changed step replaces Wu and Ding's imputation of a compatible sharp schedule by comparison of the raw multivariate-hypergeometric coefficient vector over all legal fixed schedules. Diagonal schedules fix the pooled histogram, and symmetric two-unit switches recover the arm-imbalance outer product.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing finite-population weak nulls with all-schedule histogram equivalence, common bijections, finite alphabets, and exact hypergeometric coefficients found asymptotic studentization, exact binary confidence inversion, and an i.i.d. finite-support invariance criterion, but no fixed-schedule all-\(n\), all-\(K\) classification.
seed_details.direct_evidence: The coefficient identities yield transpose pairs for \(K=2\), only the opposing endpoint pair for \(K\geq3\), and explicit legal separators. An independent raw-assignment reconstruction gives counts one and zero for the \(K=3,n=6\) cubic witness.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Wu and Ding because the weak-null randomization distribution is already characterized by their studentized theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem compares asymptotic sampling and imputation distributions and does not identify any schedule-universal finite-sample equality of observable histogram probabilities.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Theorem 1 and both orbit-counting proofs, the random-permutation extensions, and the Discussion were read. Exactness begins from an assumed group invariance and does not characterize the larger composite-null test polytope.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize the polytope of every deterministic histogram-measurable weak-null exact test by the linear size inequalities indexed by legal response tables, and determine whether an extreme point strictly power-dominates every common-orbit rank test.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace conditional uniformity on a known orbit by a finite linear feasibility system whose rows are exact hypergeometric laws of all zero-effect response tables; the new step is a facet or separation theorem for this law matrix.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found nuisance-maximized exact tests and group-orbit tests, but no extreme-point description of all weak-null histogram tests. The schedule count grows rapidly and no dimension-free facet reduction was located.
seed_details.direct_evidence: Rigdon and Hudgens and Chiba supply exact procedures outside a universal group argument, while the corner test in the presolve draft proves that the orbit subclass is strict.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from finite linear programming because exactness is just one inequality for each legal table.
seed_details.rebuttal: The finite representation is immediate, but a publishable theorem requires a nonredundant facet description and a power comparison; the search found no such reduction and the current evidence does not close it.
seed_details.decision: kept after ideation but not selected because the facet theorem remains unsupported

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Theorems 2.1--2.2, the Section 5.3 coupling construction, and the closing applications were read. Their unequal-proportion machinery is asymptotic and superpopulation-based.
seed_details.kernel: For arbitrary fixed treatment and control counts, classify the weak-null histogram-equivalence partition and decide exactly when a nonidentity common bijection survives.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Treatment complementation no longer maps the assignment space to itself, so the balanced symmetric-switch identity must be replaced by rectangular falling-factorial probes before any arm-transpose reduction is available.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for unbalanced complete-randomization automorphisms, rectangular hypergeometric coefficient equivalence, and weak-null common bijections found asymptotic robust permutation theory and binary confidence-set algorithms, but no exact partition theorem.
seed_details.direct_evidence: The loss of treatment complementation is a genuine algebraic break, and the different balanced and general complexity bounds of Aronow, Chang, and Lopatto provide an adjacent observable consequence.
seed_details.red_team: The balanced proof carries over after replacing \(m\) by the two arm sizes.
seed_details.rebuttal: The complement map changes an \(n_1\)-treated assignment into an \(n_0\)-treated assignment, so even the first universal transpose identity fails when \(n_1\neq n_0\).
seed_details.decision: kept as the first open extension

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Theorem 1 and its orbit proof, and the Discussion were read.
seed_details.kernel: Determine the smallest number of heterogeneous response types needed to separate any two inequivalent histograms, uniformly in the population size and alphabet size.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Orbit separation is constrained to transformations generated by legal zero-sum response tables; the first new step is a bounded-support integer completion of each distinguishing coefficient.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for sparse witnesses or certificate complexity in exact randomization tests found orbit counting but no heterogeneous-unit certificate number.
seed_details.direct_evidence: Two-unit switches separate all but a balanced endpoint family, a three-unit cubic gadget separates that family, and exhaustive legal-table enumeration verifies a two-unit obstruction at \(K=3,n=6\).
seed_details.red_team: This is only a proof-length refinement of the classification theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The equality of the worst-case separator number to three is an optimal certificate-complexity theorem, but it is strongest as part of the classification paper rather than as a separate angle.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Theorems 1--4 on sampling and permutation limits, the robust-interacted recommendation, and the Discussion were read. The published guarantee is sharp-null exactness plus weak-null asymptotic validity.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the exact finite-sample worst-case rejection probability of the HC2-studentized Fisher randomization test over legal finite-alphabet schedules and characterize its least-favorable tables.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the asymptotic variance comparison in Zhao and Ding by finite optimization of the assignment-dependent HC2 ratio over integer response tables.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found robust studentized weak-null asymptotics and prepivoting, but no exact finite-alphabet size envelope or least-favorable schedule theorem.
seed_details.direct_evidence: The nuisance set is finite at fixed \((n,K)\), but the HC2 denominator destroys the linear coefficient ordering used by exact binary inversion.
seed_details.red_team: Finite enumeration itself is the exact size formula.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection holds for a fixed small \(n\); without a structural optimizer or analytic envelope uniform in \(n\), the result would be computational bookkeeping.
seed_details.decision: dropped because no uniform structural reduction was verified

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, the attributable-effect and permutation-inversion constructions, Proposition 1 and its coverage argument, and the Discussion were read. The response-table search is specific to binary outcomes.
seed_details.kernel: For fixed \(K\geq3\), construct exact weak-average-score confidence sets with a polynomial test-inversion bound, or prove a complexity separation from the binary case.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The four-cell binary schedule order becomes a \(K\times K\) integer transportation table, so the first changed step is a multidimensional stochastic-order or hardness reduction for compatible schedules.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found exact binary algorithms and ordinal sharp-null tests, but no fixed-\(K\) exact weak-average-score complexity classification.
seed_details.direct_evidence: The symmetry frontier supplies a quotient of observable profiles but does not yet reduce the nuisance transportation table enough to certify polynomial complexity.
seed_details.rebuttal: A generic dynamic program may be polynomial with an exponent depending on \(K\), but neither a useful bound nor a matching lower bound is presently derived.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, exact binary inversion construction, and Discussion were read.
seed_details.kernel: Replace the equally spaced alphabet by arbitrary numerical labels and characterize which additive relations among labels create nontrivial universal histogram equivalences.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The explicit two-unit completion \(a+u=v+b\) may have no alphabet solution, so the first new step is to express separation through the additive-energy graph of the label set.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing exact weak-null randomization with Sidon sets, additive energy, and arbitrary ordinal scores found no causal classification.
seed_details.direct_evidence: The selected proof visibly uses additive completions, so nonequally spaced labels change the mechanism rather than merely notation.
seed_details.red_team: The result is just the same theorem after relabeling categories.
seed_details.rebuttal: The weak null depends on numerical differences, and relabeling changes which heterogeneous effects can cancel; nevertheless the full additive-combinatorial classification is presently too broad.
seed_details.decision: dropped as too broad for the first version

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, the main studentization theorem, the stratified extension, and the Discussion were read.
seed_details.kernel: Under independently balanced assignments within fixed strata and a single global weak null, classify the common histogram transformations induced by the product hypergeometric kernel.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Blockwise arm transposition does not preserve a merely global zero-effect restriction unless imbalance can be transferred across strata; the first step is a coupled zero-sum switch spanning two blocks.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found asymptotic stratified FRTs and exact binary confidence procedures with categorical strata, but no maximal common action under a globally coupled weak null.
seed_details.direct_evidence: The product assignment law is explicit, but the coupling of block effects creates an integer-kernel problem not resolved by the single-block proof.
seed_details.red_team: The maximal group is the direct product of the single-stratum groups.
seed_details.rebuttal: That conclusion requires a blockwise weak null; under only a global null, legal schedules couple the blocks and can destroy independent block actions.
seed_details.decision: dropped because the coupled separator theorem is unverified

seed_details.anchor_read: The Introduction, Theorem 1 and its orbit-stabilizer proof, and the Discussion were read.
seed_details.kernel: For matched pairs with finite-alphabet outcomes and a global zero-average-effect null, characterize the maximal schedule-universal sign-change subgroup on pair summaries.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The usual pairwise sign-flip group assumes pairwise exchangeability; the first changed step is to intersect its invariance relations over schedules satisfying only one global effect equation.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found matched-pair randomization inference and exact binary confidence algorithms, but no common-group classification under a global rather than pairwise sharp null.
seed_details.direct_evidence: The distinction between pairwise and global restrictions is clear, but no sparse separating family has been derived.
seed_details.red_team: Without pairwise sharpness every nonidentity sign flip plainly fails.
seed_details.rebuttal: Endpoint saturation can create exceptional equal-probability profiles, so the identity conclusion is not immediate; current evidence is insufficient to classify all exceptions.

seed:alphabet-symmetry-frontier: Wu and Ding (2021, Theorem 1 and Section 8) show that a studentized Fisher randomization distribution is asymptotically conservative for a weak finite-population null; their finite-sample exactness remains attached to a compatible sharp null.
Hemerik and Goeman (2018, Theorem 1) derive exact rank tests conditional on a given finite-group invariance and orbit, but do not derive the invariance common to a composite causal null.

Dutz and Zhang (2026, Proposition 2.5) reduce existence of a randomization hypothesis to a nontrivial invariant bijection, and Proposition 3.1 turns i.i.d. finite-support invariance into equality of probability monomials. Their law is an i.i.d. product distribution rather than a fixed response table under complete assignment.

Rigdon and Hudgens (2015, Sections 2--3) and Li and Ding (2016) obtain exact binary average-effect confidence sets by prediction or nuisance-table test inversion; they do not classify equality of observable probabilities across every compatible schedule.

Aronow, Chang, and Lopatto (2025, Theorem 4.1 and Section 5) reduce the number of permutation tests needed for binary exact confidence sets, with a balanced-versus-general complexity split, but do not characterize schedule-universal histogram actions.

No closer primary source located through 12 September 2026 states the all-\(n\), all-\(K\) fixed-schedule equivalence partition, its maximal common bijection group, or the sharp three-heterogeneous-unit certificate.
seed:exact-test-polytope: Hemerik and Goeman (2018) characterize the orbit-rank subclass once group invariance is assumed.
Dufour (2006) supplies exact nuisance-maximization logic for discrete tests but not a facet description of the weak-null response-table law matrix.
Rigdon and Hudgens (2015) and Chiba (2015) furnish feasible binary exact procedures, confirming that failure of a rich common group is not an impossibility theorem for exact testing.
The exact polytope remains unoccupied in the located literature, but its nonredundant facet structure is not yet supported strongly enough for selection.
seed:unbalanced-rectangular-frontier: Romano (1990) shows that permutation behavior without genuine invariance changes materially with allocation balance.
Chung and Romano (2013) use multinomial--hypergeometric coupling for unequal proportions to obtain asymptotic robustness, not a finite-population causal orbit classification.
Aronow, Chang, and Lopatto (2025) prove different exact-confidence computational bounds for balanced and general complete randomization.
No located result subsumes the rectangular all-schedule equivalence question; it is retained as the concrete open extension rather than asserted in the headline.
